study.title: Deep brain stimulation reshapes memory cell assemblies and drives distinct transcriptional programs in human cortex

cover.headline: Brain stimulation may work by **rewriting which genes a cell switches on**, not just firing it.

slides.title: If electricity edits gene programs, stimulation could be tuned rather than simply turned up.
slides.body:
Clinical stimulators are set by dose: more current, more relief. If the real lever is which gene program a pulse starts, timing might matter more than strength.

That would be a different dial, and nobody has built it.

slides.title: Stimulation tightened the neuron gangs that hold a memory, and woke the support cells.
slides.body:
They mapped 19 cell assemblies, the neuron clusters that hold one memory. After stimulation those clusters fired in tighter lockstep.

Separate gene programs switched on in neurons and in astrocytes, the support cells long written off as glue.

stat.label: memory cell assemblies mapped and tracked

slides.title: They waited for patients already in epilepsy surgery and read the living tissue directly.
slides.body:
You cannot ethically take cortex from a volunteer. Twelve people having epilepsy surgery agreed to have a patch of temporal cortex stimulated and then sampled.

That is why the number is twelve, and why it is human tissue at all.

caveats: Only twelve people, all with epilepsy, which is a brain already behaving unusually.
They sampled temporal cortex. Clinical stimulation targets deeper structures this study never touched.
This captures hours of stimulation. Real patients get years, and nobody knows what that does.

cta.headline: Send this to anyone who thinks brain stimulation is crude
cta.sub: One real study, every weekday. The full paper is linked in bio.

caption: Brain stimulation may not just fire neurons. It may change which genes they switch on, in living human cortex.
